lesson.menu_title: Making the Ask at the Table
lesson.menu_desc: The bank has answered: two yeses and one no. Today you learn the shapes that let the other side say yes -- could you, would you be able to, I would like you to -- plus what you offer in return and where you hold firm -- 32 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 14 -- Making the Ask
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Sergio Takashi Tanaka | Lesson 14 -- Making the Ask

paras: Dear Sergio, thank you for your note of Tuesday and for setting out your three asks so clearly. I took them to our credit committee this morning, and I would like to give you an answer on each one before we speak on Thursday.

On the ceiling, we can move, but not all the way. The committee has granted an increase to one hundred and eighty million. That is below your benchmark, and I know it, but it is well above the number we opened with. On the grace period, the answer is yes. We would be happy to give you six months before the first payment, and nobody here sees a problem with that.

On the arrangement fee, I have to hold firm. One percent is what we charge every client of your size, and dropping it for one name would be very hard to explain internally. Would you be able to accept the fee if we meet you halfway on the ceiling? In return, I can put the grace period in writing the same day you sign.

One last thing, and please read it in the right tone. Do not take the fee as a hard no on everything. We have three years of goodwill with your desk, and nobody on this side wants you to walk away over a number this small. Could you send me your view before Thursday morning, so that I can prepare the committee? I would like to close the whole package on the call.

listenings.text: Hi Sergio, it is Marina. A quick note before Thursday. I read Nordbank's reply twice. Three asks went out and two of them came back in a shape we can live with, so let us be very clear about which one still matters. The ceiling is the one you cannot drop. The grace period is already granted and the fee is small, so do not spend the call on either of them. On the fee, my view is simple. Give it to them. Say we accept the one percent, and in return ask them to take the ceiling to our benchmark and to put the grace period in writing the day we sign. That is a clean trade and he can sell it to his committee. Where you hold firm is the ceiling, and only the ceiling. One more thing. Please do not use the words walk away on this call. Keep that card in your pocket. We play it only if the number is still there on Friday, and even then I want to hear it from you first. Good luck.

Sergio, it is Paulo from the credit desk. One thought about Thursday, and it is not about the numbers. The way you phrase the ask decides how much room the other side has to say yes. If you say we need the ceiling at two hundred, that is an order, and the poor man on the other end has to defend a position instead of solving a problem. If you say would you be able to take the ceiling to two hundred, he can walk into his committee and argue for you. Same number, completely different conversation. Second thing, the package. Never ask for three things one at a time, because they say no three times and then there is nothing left to trade. Put them on the table together and say which one matters most. And the last thing, about goodwill. Thank him for the grace period before you push on the ceiling. It costs you nothing and it buys you the tone for the rest of the call. Talk on Friday.

extra_audio.text: First, thank the other side for what they have already granted. Then put all your asks on the table together, not one at a time. Next, say which one matters most and why. After that, offer something in return, so they can sell the answer internally. Finally, ask for a clear next step and a date.
